conventions.convention: The punctures have increasing real coordinates, the boundary basepoint is d=(0,1), stems are straight, and meridians and the boundary loop are counterclockwise. The boundary word is x1⋯xn.
Automorphism products are ordinary composition, with the rightmost factor acting first. The positive Artin generator sends xi to xi xi+1 xi⁻¹ and xi+1 to xi.
Peripheral preservation uses conjugates of positive basis generators; boundary preservation fixes the ordered product itself, not merely its conjugacy class.

Puncture-ended arc homotopies extend continuously over the compact parameter square in the filled disk, with interior tracks avoiding marked points. The isotopy conclusion concerns unoriented images at coincident endpoints and parametrized arcs at distinct ordered endpoints; AC is assumed.
The LKB space is unordered two-point configuration in the closed punctured disk. Its base configuration consists of two distinct lower-boundary points, ordered left to right.
The LKB representation acts on ordinary absolute integral H2. Deck translations act on the left over Λ=Z[q±1,t±1]; relative groups are auxiliary pairing modules.
Natural relative maps run from smaller end radii to larger radii. The direct limits toward zero use their canonical inverses after stabilization.

The unprimed pairing is absolute versus boundary-plus-end-relative; the primed pairing is end-relative versus boundary-only-relative. Coefficients in the second argument are conjugated by q↦q⁻¹,t↦t⁻¹.
Deck monomials are ordered lexicographically with the q-exponent first. Geometric labelled terms remain distinct before equal monomials are collected.
Links and ambient isotopies are smooth; parametrizations and component labels are ignored, while component orientations are preserved. The empty link is admitted.

Closure uses the fixed framing φ([(x,t)])=(√(1−|x|²)e^(2πit),x). Components follow endpoint-permutation cycles and increasing page parameter. General continuous braids use selected smooth models under countable choice.
Coherent circles agree with annulus boundary orientations in opposite senses. Height counts every incoherent unordered pair, including pairs without a crossing arc.
Ordinary stabilization adds a rightmost strand and a final signed generator, for n≥1. B0 is an isolated Markov class. Geometric time traverses the rightmost factor first.
For n≥3, the absolute LKB lattice and the Krammer matrix lattice are compared over Q(q,t), not by an integral equivariant identification. The parameter translation is tKrammer=−tBigelow.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For every n≥1 the Artin representation ρ:Bn→Aut(Fn) is injective; equivalently, a braid word acts trivially on Fn only if it represents the trivial braid.

Assume AC. Simple proper arcs with the same boundary or puncture endpoints, homotopic relative to endpoints through the specified compactly extended proper arcs, are isotopic as unoriented images; distinct ordered endpoints also permit an isotopy of their parametrizations.

For absolute x and boundary-plus-end-relative y, the displayed Laurent intersection sum has finite support, depends only on homology classes, is Λ-sesquilinear and is invariant under simultaneous braid action; the same assertions hold for the primed pairing.

For n≥1, ordinary absolute H2 of the winding cover is the kernel of the displayed two-dimensional cellular differential. Its natural fraction-field localization is injective and has dimension binomial(n,2); integral freeness and injection into end-relative homology are not asserted.
If coefficients cij∈Q(q,t) give v=Σ cij vij in H2 of the LKB cover with integral coefficients, then every cij lies in Λ; equivalently the closed surfaces vij span the absolute integral module over Λ.
Assume AC and positive minimal tine–noodle intersection count. A maximal monomial mij equals mii and mjj; all terms carrying a maximal monomial have the same sign, so its coefficient is nonzero.

Assume countable choice. A smooth link isotopy stationary near its regular-projection endpoints admits arbitrarily close endpoint-relative perturbations with finitely many ordinary cusps, nondegenerate double tangencies and transverse triple events, at distinct times, no quadruple points, and planar isotopy on regular intervals.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. If D′ is obtained from D by a Yamada–Vogel reducing move, then h(D′)=h(D)−1. Consequently every reducing sequence starting at D has length at most h(D).

Assume AC. For n≥m≥0 and arbitrary α∈Bn, the specified last-band packet Qm,m Tm⁻¹ reduces to α by conjugations and exactly m positive ordinary destabilizations. Its generator mirror gives the negative version; the reverse-order packet Tm Qm,m⁻¹ gives exactly m negative destabilizations. Reversing gives the corresponding stabilizations.

Assume AC. For c,p,q≥0, arbitrary P∈B(c+p), Q∈B(c+q), and the stated shifted placements, P Qp,q Q Qp,q⁻¹ and P Qq,p⁻¹ Q Qq,p are related by a finite ordinary Markov sequence. Zero-width endpoints coincide.

Assume AC. The two height-zero reductions of the irreducible four-band d-pair produce closed braids whose words differ by braid isotopies and ordinary Markov stabilizations and destabilizations; uniform reducing-choice ambiguity is resolved by a band exchange.

For the reduced conjugator expressions of a peripheral-boundary-preserving automorphism, either no adjacent junction cancellation deletes a middle letter and the automorphism is identity, or the least qualifying junction has V=RaU when its left middle letter is deleted first, and U=Rb⁻¹V when its right middle letter is deleted first.

concerns.concern: The exponent-sum form says that forgetting punctures gives a braid in B2 and identifies its σ1 exponent b with the positive winding exponent. Under the published identification Φgeo(β)=(ι*[S(β)])⁻¹, a raw positive mobile half-rotation loop corresponds to σ1⁻¹: its winding exponent is +1 but its Artin exponent is −1. The same sign issue affects b′ and a=(b′−b)/2. The winding definition itself is coherent. Adjudicate which loop-to-braid identification this paragraph intends; an alternative raw-slicing convention must be stated explicitly rather than silently using the published group isomorphism.

F3 gives Φ the codomain π1(Cn(D°),[Q]) but defines Φ(β)=(ι*[S(β)])⁻¹. The cited theorem makes ι* land in π1(Cn(D²),[Q]), so that displayed codomain is mistyped. Proof 1.1 correctly distinguishes applying the inclusion from inversion; the conjugacy argument survives.

Unresolved source-verification obligation, not a finding that the word identities are false: steps 2.2–4.2 identify Traczyk Figure 8 panels with specific chronological records, shifts, signs and full-twist placements. I read the complete relevant textual argument at https://scispace.com/pdf/a-new-proof-of-markov-s-braid-theorem-z9a08ypli9.pdf, printed pp. 415–419, and the survey's Lemma 2.8 discussion at https://www.math.columbia.edu/~jb/Handbook-21.pdf. The original PDF returned 403, the archive fetch failed, and figure rendering for both recovered sources returned cache miss; an in-memory shell retrieval failed DNS. Consequently I could not independently check the visual panel-to-word transcription, including the Example 5_2 source picture. The algebraic suppliers and their stated placements were read, but source figures still need visual inspection before accepting that geometric identification.
